senses.def: not excited, nervous, or upset
examples: Try to stay calm and explain what happened.
She remained calm even when the plane started shaking.

senses.def: without strong wind or big waves
examples: The sea was calm enough for swimming.

senses.def: to make someone or something quieter and more relaxed
examples: The mayor tried to calm angry residents at the meeting.
Calm down, it's not a big deal.

senses.def: a quiet, peaceful time or situation
examples: A strange calm settled over the city after the protests.

note: The l is silent in American English: /kɑːm/. Saying "calm down" to an angry person can sound rude.

senses.def: a device for taking photographs or recording video
examples: My phone's camera takes better pictures than my old digital one.
Security cameras recorded the robbery.

note: "On camera" = being filmed. "Off camera" = not being filmed. Usually two syllables in speech: /ˈkæmrə/.

senses.def: a place where people stay in tents or simple buildings for a short time
examples: We set up camp next to the river.
Thousands of refugees are living in camps near the border.

senses.def: (American) a place where children go in summer to do activities
examples: The kids are going to summer camp for two weeks.

senses.def: to stay in a tent for a short time, usually for fun
examples: We camped in the mountains for three nights.

note: "Camp" can also mean a group with the same opinion: the two camps in the debate.

senses.def: a series of planned activities to achieve a political, social, or business goal
examples: The company launched an advertising campaign for its new phone.
Her election campaign focused on health care.

senses.def: to work in an organized way to achieve something or to win an election
examples: Parents are campaigning for safer roads near the school.
He campaigned in every state before the election.

note: The g is silent: /kæmˈpeɪn/.

senses.def: the activity of staying in a tent or simple shelter, usually on vacation
examples: We go camping in Yosemite every summer.
Bring warm clothes; camping in the desert gets cold at night.

note: In Turkish "kamping" means a campsite; in English "camping" is the activity. The place is a "campsite" or "campground".

senses.def: the buildings and land of a university, college, or company
examples: First-year students are required to live on campus.
The company's new campus has its own gym and cafeteria.

note: Say "on campus", not "in campus". Plural: campuses.

senses.def: used to say that someone is able to do something or that something is possible
examples: She can speak four languages.
Smoking can cause serious health problems.

senses.def: used to ask for or give permission, or to make a request
examples: Can I use your phone for a minute?
You can leave early today if you want.

senses.def: a metal container for food or drink
examples: He opened a can of soda and sat down.

note: Past: could. Negative: cannot / can't. British English often says "tin" for a food can.

senses.def: a long artificial waterway for boats or for carrying water
examples: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
Venice is famous for its canals.

senses.def: a tube inside the body that carries food, air, or other substances
examples: The dentist said I need a root canal.

note: A TV "kanal" is a "channel" in English, not a canal.

senses.def: to decide that something arranged will not happen
examples: Our flight was canceled because of the snowstorm.
I had to cancel my dentist appointment.

senses.def: to end an agreement, order, or subscription
examples: I canceled my gym membership after two months.

note: American spelling: canceled, canceling (British: cancelled). "Cancel out" means balance so there is no effect.

senses.def: a serious disease in which cells in the body grow in an uncontrolled way
examples: Smoking is the leading cause of lung cancer.
Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer last year.

senses.def: a person who is trying to be elected or who is applying for a job
examples: Three candidates are running for mayor.
We interviewed ten candidates for the position.

senses.def: someone or something likely to be chosen for something
examples: The old factory is a strong candidate for redevelopment.

senses.def: a stick of wax with a string in the middle that you burn to give light
examples: She blew out the candles on her birthday cake.
We lit candles when the power went out.

note: "Burn the candle at both ends" means work too hard and sleep too little.

senses.def: the negative form of can
examples: I cannot believe how quickly the year went by.
Visitors cannot enter the building without an ID.

note: Written as one word. "Can't" is the usual spoken form; "cannot" is more formal or emphatic.

senses.def: a strong, heavy cloth used for tents, bags, and shoes
examples: He wore old canvas sneakers.
The tent was made of thick canvas.

senses.def: a piece of this cloth used for painting on, or a painting on it
examples: The artist stretched a large canvas over a wooden frame.

note: "Canvass" (double s) is a different word: to ask people for votes or opinions.

senses.def: a soft, flat hat with a hard curved part at the front
examples: He always wears a baseball cap backward.

senses.def: a cover that protects the end of a pen, bottle, or tube
examples: Put the cap back on the toothpaste.

senses.def: an upper limit on an amount of money
examples: The city placed a cap on rent increases.

senses.def: to put a limit on an amount
examples: Interest rates on student loans are capped at five percent.

note: "To cap it all" means "as the final bad thing".

senses.def: the ability or power to do something
examples: The new software has the capability to translate in real time.
Some countries are developing nuclear capability.

note: Common in plural for skills or features: the phone's camera capabilities.

senses.def: having the ability or power to do something
examples: The stadium is capable of holding fifty thousand people.
I'm perfectly capable of making my own decisions.

senses.def: good at your work; skilled
examples: She's a very capable manager.

note: Pattern: capable OF doing something, not "capable to do".

senses.def: the number of people or things that a place or container can hold
examples: The concert hall has a capacity of two thousand.
The hospital is already full to capacity.

senses.def: the ability to understand or do something
examples: Children have an amazing capacity for learning languages.

senses.def: an official position or role
examples: She attended the meeting in her capacity as company lawyer.

senses.def: the city where a country's government is based
examples: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, not Istanbul.

senses.def: money or property used to start a business or to invest
examples: They raised enough capital to open a second restaurant.

senses.def: (of a letter) in the large form used at the start of a sentence or name
examples: Names of countries always start with a capital letter.

senses.def: involving the death penalty
examples: Capital punishment was abolished in many states.

note: Don't confuse with "Capitol", the building where the US Congress meets.

senses.def: an economic system in which businesses are owned privately and run for profit
examples: Critics argue that capitalism increases inequality.
The country moved from communism to capitalism in the 1990s.

senses.def: based on or supporting capitalism
examples: Most Western countries have capitalist economies.
The book criticizes capitalist values.

senses.def: a person who supports capitalism or who owns a lot of business wealth
examples: Venture capitalists invested millions in the startup.

senses.def: the person in charge of a ship or plane
examples: The captain announced that we would land in twenty minutes.

senses.def: the leader of a sports team
examples: She was named captain of the soccer team.

senses.def: an officer of middle rank in the army, navy, or police
examples: A police captain spoke to reporters outside the station.

senses.def: to catch a person or animal, or to take control of a place by force
examples: Police captured the suspect after a two-day search.
Rebels captured the city's airport.

senses.def: to record or show something accurately in words, pictures, or film
examples: The photo perfectly captures the joy of the moment.

senses.def: the act of catching or being caught
examples: The soldier managed to avoid capture for weeks.

senses.def: a road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a few people
examples: She drives an old car to work every day.
We rented a car at the airport.

senses.def: (American) a separate part of a train
examples: The dining car is at the back of the train.

note: "Get in/out of a car", but "get on/off a bus or train". British "car park" = American "parking lot".

senses.def: a chemical element found in all living things, and in coal, diamonds, and graphite
examples: Diamonds are made of pure carbon.
Trees absorb carbon from the air.

senses.def: carbon dioxide or other carbon gases, especially as a cause of climate change
examples: The city plans to cut carbon emissions by half by 2035.

note: Your "carbon footprint" is the amount of carbon dioxide your activities produce. "Carbonated" drinks are fizzy.

senses.def: a folded piece of stiff paper with a message, sent on special occasions
examples: I sent my grandmother a birthday card.

senses.def: a small plastic card used for paying or identifying yourself
examples: Can I pay by card?
Show your ID card at the entrance.

senses.def: one of a set of cards used for playing games
examples: We stayed up late playing cards.

note: "Put your cards on the table" = be honest about your plans. "In the cards" (American) = likely to happen.

senses.def: to feel that something is important or to be worried about it
examples: I don't care what other people think.
He really cares about the environment.

senses.def: to look after someone who is sick, young, or old (care for)
examples: She quit her job to care for her elderly father.

senses.def: the process of looking after someone and providing what they need
examples: The patients receive excellent care at this hospital.

senses.def: attention and effort to avoid damage or mistakes
examples: Handle the package with care; it's fragile.

note: "Take care" also means goodbye. "I couldn't care less" means "I don't care at all".

senses.def: the series of jobs someone has in one area of work over their life
examples: She began her career as a reporter in Chicago.
He's thinking about a career in medicine.

note: Stress on the second syllable: ca-REER. Don't confuse with "carrier".

senses.def: giving attention to what you are doing to avoid accidents or mistakes
examples: Be careful crossing the street.
You need to be careful with your money.

senses.def: done with a lot of attention to detail
examples: After careful consideration, we decided not to move.

senses.def: with a lot of attention to avoid mistakes, damage, or danger
examples: Read the instructions carefully before you start.
He carefully placed the vase on the shelf.

senses.def: not giving enough attention to what you are doing, so that you make mistakes
examples: I lost points on the test because of careless mistakes.
It was careless of you to leave the door unlocked.

senses.def: the goods carried by a ship, plane, or truck
examples: The ship was carrying a cargo of grain to Egypt.
Cargo planes land at the airport throughout the night.

note: Turkish "kargo" usually means a parcel delivery; in English that is a "package" or "delivery", not cargo.

senses.def: thick material that covers a floor
examples: We're replacing the old carpet with wood floors.
Take your shoes off so you don't get mud on the carpet.

senses.def: a thick layer of something on the ground
examples: A carpet of autumn leaves covered the path.

note: A "rug" covers part of a floor; "carpet" usually covers it all. "Roll out the red carpet" = welcome someone grandly.

senses.def: a vehicle pulled by horses, used especially in the past
examples: Tourists can ride a horse-drawn carriage through Central Park.

senses.def: (British) a separate section of a train for passengers
examples: The first carriage was packed, so we walked to the back.

senses.def: (American) a baby carriage, a small vehicle for pushing a baby
examples: She pushed the baby carriage slowly through the park.

note: For a train section, Americans say "car" and the British say "carriage". A modern baby carriage is usually called a "stroller".

senses.def: a long, pointed orange vegetable that grows under the ground
examples: Chop the carrots and add them to the soup.
Kids often eat raw carrots as a snack.

senses.def: something offered to persuade someone to do something
examples: The government is using tax breaks as a carrot to attract investors.

note: "Carrot and stick" means using both rewards and punishments (Turkish: havuç ve sopa).

senses.def: to hold something and take it from one place to another
examples: Can you help me carry these boxes upstairs?
The bus carries about fifty passengers.

senses.def: to have something with you all the time
examples: I always carry an umbrella in my bag.

senses.def: to involve something as a result or a risk
examples: The crime carries a sentence of up to ten years in prison.

note: "Carry out" = do or complete (carry out research). "Carry on" = continue. "Get carried away" = become too excited.

senses.def: a film or TV show made from drawings, usually for children
examples: My kids watch cartoons every Saturday morning.

senses.def: a funny drawing in a newspaper or magazine, often about politics
examples: The newspaper published a cartoon mocking the senator.

note: A "caricature" exaggerates a real person's features; a "cartoon" is broader.

senses.def: to make an object or pattern by cutting wood, stone, or another hard material
examples: He carved a small bird out of a piece of wood.
Someone carved their initials into the tree.

senses.def: to cut cooked meat into slices
examples: Dad always carves the turkey on Thanksgiving.

senses.def: to create a position or reputation through hard work (carve out)
examples: She has carved out a successful career in tech.

note: "Carved in stone" means fixed and impossible to change: The plan isn't carved in stone.

senses.def: a particular situation or example of something
examples: In some cases, patients recover without any treatment.
Take an umbrella in case it rains.

senses.def: a matter decided in court, or a crime investigated by the police
examples: The case will go to trial next month.
Detectives are still working on the case.

senses.def: an example of a disease or illness
examples: There have been thousands of new flu cases this week.

senses.def: a container or cover that protects something
examples: I need a new case for my phone.

note: "In case" = as a precaution (take a coat in case it gets cold), not the same as "if". "Make a case for" = argue in favor of.

senses.def: money in the form of coins and bills
examples: Do you take cash or only cards?
I don't carry much cash anymore.

senses.def: to exchange a check for money
examples: I need to cash this check at the bank.

note: Uncountable: "a lot of cash". "Cash in on" means profit from a situation, often unfairly.

senses.def: a building where people play games for money, such as cards or roulette
examples: They lost a lot of money at a casino in Las Vegas.
The new casino brought jobs but also problems to the town.

note: Turkish "gazino" is usually a music venue; the English "casino" is only for gambling.

senses.def: all the actors in a play, movie, or TV show
examples: The movie has an amazing cast of young actors.

senses.def: to look in a direction, or to make light, a shadow, or doubt fall on something
examples: She cast a quick glance at the clock.
The new evidence casts doubt on his story.

senses.def: to vote
examples: Over a million people cast their votes by mail.

senses.def: to choose an actor for a particular role
examples: She was cast as the lead in the new series.

note: Irregular: cast – cast – cast. A "cast" is also the hard cover put on a broken arm or leg (alçı).

senses.def: a large, strong building with thick walls and towers, built in the past for defense
examples: We visited a medieval castle on top of the hill.
The kids built a sand castle on the beach.

note: The t is silent: /ˈkæsl/. "Build castles in the air" means make unrealistic plans.

senses.def: relaxed and not formal
examples: You can wear casual clothes to the office on Fridays.
It was a casual dinner with a few friends.

senses.def: not showing much care or interest
examples: His casual attitude toward safety worried the team.

senses.def: not regular or serious; happening by chance
examples: To a casual observer, the two paintings look identical.

note: "Business casual" is a dress code: neat but not a suit and tie.

senses.def: a person who is killed or injured in a war or accident
examples: The earthquake caused heavy casualties.
There were no casualties in the fire, thanks to the alarm.

senses.def: someone or something that suffers as a result of an event
examples: Small shops were the first casualties of the recession.

note: Includes both injured and killed people. "Fatality" means only someone who died.

senses.def: a small furry animal often kept as a pet
examples: Our cat sleeps on the sofa all afternoon.
Istanbul is famous for its street cats.

senses.def: a large wild animal of the cat family
examples: Lions and tigers are the best-known big cats.

collocations: let the cat out of the bag
note: "Let the cat out of the bag" means reveal a secret by accident.

senses.def: a complete list of items, such as products for sale or books in a library
examples: The store sends out a new catalog every season.
You can search the library's online catalog.

senses.def: a long series of bad things
examples: The report describes a catalog of errors by hospital staff.

senses.def: to make a list of things in an organized way
examples: Volunteers are cataloging thousands of old photographs.

note: American spelling: catalog. British spelling: catalogue.

senses.def: to stop and hold a moving object, or to capture a person or animal
examples: The dog jumped up to catch the ball.
Police finally managed to catch the thief.

senses.def: to get on a bus, train, or plane before it leaves
examples: I have to catch the 7:15 train.

senses.def: to get an illness
examples: Wear a coat or you'll catch a cold.

senses.def: the act of catching something; also a hidden problem
examples: What a great catch by the goalkeeper!
The flights are so cheap; what's the catch?

note: Irregular verb: catch – caught – caught. "Catch up" = reach the same level; "catch on" = become popular.

senses.def: a group of people or things with similar features
examples: The film was nominated in three categories.
Most of our customers fall into the 25 to 40 age category.

note: "Categorically" means completely and definitely: He categorically denied the claims.

senses.tr: (yemek ve içecek) hizmeti vermek, catering yapmak
senses.def: to provide food and drinks for a party or event
examples: A local restaurant catered the wedding.
The company caters for events of up to five hundred people.

senses.def: to provide what a particular group of people needs or wants (cater to)
examples: The hotel caters to business travelers.

note: American English prefers "cater to"; British English uses "cater for". "Cater to" can also mean satisfy demands too much.
